prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: Cn1ncnc1[C@H]1c2n[nH]c(=O)c3cc(F)cc(c23)N[C@@H]1c1ccc(F)cc1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL3105

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of human PARP1 using [3H]NAD as substrate after 1 min by microplate scintillation counting analysis
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of PARP1 (unknown origin) by ELISA
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "INSUFFICIENT_INFO", "confidence": 0.5, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "The two assays use fundamentally different detection methods (scintillation counting with radiolabeled NAD vs. ELISA), which can yield different IC50 values depending on substrate concentrations, incubation times, and assay formats, but without knowing the specific conditions and the protein construct origin in Assay B, it is uncertain whether results will agree within 0.3 log units or diverge beyond 1.0 log units."}
